summary: Implement the frozen secrets/security capability with opaque tenant-bound references, a provider port, local AES-GCM encryption, rotation/revocation semantics, shared redaction helpers, and a PostgreSQL ciphertext adapter without introducing a new architecture pillar.

impacts.evidence: Secret references and ciphertext versions carry organization/workspace scope, use forced RLS, and the connector-account reference uses a composite tenant-bound foreign key.
Provider credentials are isolated from ordinary tables and durable analytics surfaces; shared redaction helpers classify credential-shaped keys and values before audit/log persistence.
Task 021 adds no REST operation or OpenAPI endpoint; the JSON Schema describes internal-safe reference metadata rather than a new public API route.
No event family or envelope changes are introduced and secret material remains explicitly prohibited from Kafka/event payloads.
This task establishes the internal SecretProvider boundary consumed later by Connector SDK Task 010; it does not yet publish or change the plugin SDK.
Atomic migration 000005 adds secret reference/ciphertext tables, connector-account reference wiring, forced RLS, immutable-version guards, and catalog history.

AES-256-GCM, external master-key sourcing, AEAD tenant/reference binding, fixed consumer errors, buffer wiping, immutable ciphertext versions, revocation, and no plaintext credential columns form the core security boundary.
Secret rotation/revocation is implemented but this task does not define approval policy; sensitive-operation approval enforcement remains owned by Task 017 and later governance work.
Audit/log redaction now reuse the shared secrets classifier; only opaque references and safe lifecycle metadata may be audited while credential material is excluded.
Secret lifecycle uses optimistic version checks but does not define commerce reconciliation, inbox deduplication, or external delivery idempotency.
Webhook signing secrets become a supported class, but delivery/egress behavior is unchanged and no credential leaves the provider boundary.
No SLO/metric/trace contract is added; logging behavior only centralizes the existing credential-redaction classifier.
Migration 000005 is expand-only but classified high risk and requires a backup checkpoint; master-key recovery remains external to PostgreSQL backup/restore.

Unit tests cover encryption/lifecycle/key rollover/wiping/tenant binding and redaction; migration/static/runtime smoke covers RLS, ciphertext immutability, tenant isolation, connector reference FKs, and forbidden plaintext columns.
